ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and black-bordered lateral stripes. A prominent pale collar marks the neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Anguiculus rappii* is best distinguished by the prominent, pale yellow or white stripe running along the center of its neck, which contrasts sharply with its dark body.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Stripe-necked Snake inhabits moist, temperate broadleaf forests and shrublands within the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Stripe-necked Snake is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small prey like lizards and frogs along forest edges and rocky stream banks during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Anguiculus rappii* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Anguiculus rappii* is endemic to the Western Himalayas, primarily occurring in the states of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand at elevations between 1,500 and 2,700 meters.
